units.translation: to the hearth of the god Phoebus.
you hold the altar, the hearth of the land.
For the sheep of the central hearth already stand,
as long as Aegisthus keeps the fire burning on my hearth.
having come as a suppliant to the hearth.
I honor the unheated hearth of the house.
nor to turn to another hearth (thus Turnebus corrected for ephestion).
someone sitting in the house by the hearth.
nor having rushed from the hearth.
the griefs in the house at the hearth.
when you came to the hearth of the house.
O saviors of the paternal hearth.
when he drives all pollution from the hearth.

where it can mean nothing other than one who stays at the hearth or at home, if μόνον [only] is correctly read, which Musgrave wanted to change to ψόλον [smoke], and Dobree in Adversaria vol. 2 p. 31 to δόμων [of the house].
they have come, having fled – to the land that holds the hearth.
For if I see any one who keeps the hearth, only one, I will set fire to the roof, letting loose a torrential flame.
they sacrificed on the hearth of fire.
the furthest place of the earth.
on the furthest borders of the land.
there is a city, Canobus, the furthest of the land.
But, with Hermann, I preferred to write ἔσω [within] rather than in the antistrophe v. 812 ξυλλάβοιτο [may he take part] for ξυλλάβοι [may he take].
my heart is stirred from within.
the self-taught heart within sings the dirge of the Fury.
the one within (thus Seidler for ἔσω) the halls.
the length of a year's watch.
and contracted Ἐτεοκλῆς [Eteocles], who comes on stage in the Seven against Thebes.

at the beginning of the trimeter the third syllable is long rather than short, and likewise 39 Ἐτεόκλεες, φέριστε Καδμείων ἄναξ [Eteocles, bravest lord of the Cadmeans], and 1007 Ἐτεοκλέα μὲν τόνδ᾽ ἐπ᾿ εὐνοίᾳ χθονὸς θάπτειν ἔδοξε [it was decided to bury this Eteocles for his goodwill to the land].
the corrector wrote in the margin of M Ἐτεόκλεις ἀρχηγέτα [Eteocles, leader].
Eteocles, bravest lord of the Cadmeans
it was decided to bury this Eteocles for his goodwill to the land
For third, for Eteoclus, the third lot leapt from the upturned bronze-cheeked helmet.
giving victory to one side, aiding one party
aiding others, bringing help to one side.
where the scholiast explains it by νικηφόρος [victory-bringing]. It is a Homeric word, on which see Thesaurus vol. 3 p. 2125.
Ares, giver of victory to one side
turning or inclining to one side.
he will beget another avenger upon his head from that one.
to bend back the other leg of the double course.
I will present you with one of two choices.
he will wish for one of two things.
